thread:
infra-bot: :rotating_light: autopilot-detect: Rapid scale oscillation detected in eu-west-1 - high pod churn, repeated node evictions, service: serving-runtime-prod. Alerts: autoscaler thrash + CUDA OOM spikes.

sasha: I'm on it. getting logs now. tagging @lee for runtime.

lee: ack. looking at node events, seeing repeated kubelet eviction cycles. suspect autoscaler bounce is causing warmup IO + cuda memory fragmentation -> OOMs.

devon: seeing a cascade: autoscaler adds nodes, pods scheduled, kubelet bootstraps, containers init heavy model load -> OOM during model load -> crashloop -> node marked unhealthy -> autoscaler removes nodes -> repeat.

nora: customer-facing impact? support-ops, any reports?

support-ops: multiple customers in EU reporting elevated 5xx and long tail latency on generation endpoints since ~2123456750. Ticket rate spike ~3x. Some teams routed to fallback models but not all.

lee: quick mitigation plan: 1) throttle autoscaler aggressive up/down - increase stabilizationWindow and scaleDownDelay 2) pin model variants to quantized light variants for new pods 3) cordon a subset of nodes to stop churn and move stable workloads there 4) enable fallback to cpu-backed small models for low tier traffic.

sasha: executing step 1 now - bumping cluster-autoscaler flags. running: `kubectl patch deploy cluster-autoscaler -n kube-system --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/args/3","value":"--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m"}]'`

infra-bot: deploy-bot: cluster-autoscaler patched by sasha at 2123456810.

devon: pinned serving profiles for the heavy model to quantized-x6 variant via configmap: `serving-models-configmap` update. rolling update triggered.

lee: cordoning nodes eu-west-1a/02 and 03 to stabilize: `kubectl cordon node/eu-west-1a-02` then drain non-critical system pods.

nora: paging customers impacted: internal status page draft: "We are investigating increased errors in eu-west; engineering is actively mitigating. " Going to post updates every 15m.

sasha: starting canary route to dedicated-stable-pool for 10% traffic to test stability. `rbac: routing rule update -> weight 10%`

devon: logs from a crashed container snippet: ```
2026-02-10T09:14:22Z stderr F RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.5 GiB (GPU 0; 31.75 GiB total capacity; 28.00 GiB already allocated; 2.25 GiB free; 25.00 GiB reserved)
  File "/app/serve/loader.py", line 412, in load_weights
    model.load_state_dict(checkpoint)
```

lee: seeing repeated OOMs during cold starts, and Gpu kernel retry logs: `GPU driver: context lost` then container restarts. When nodes go Unhealthy, kube autoscaler reduces capacity -> oscillation.

kyle: adding damping to autoscaler policy now: set `--scan-interval=60s` and `--expander=least-waste` to avoid aggressive add/remove.

infra-bot: autoscaler flags updated by kyle at 2123456830.

devon: rolling restart of runtime pods on stabilized nodes complete. Canary traffic on stable-pool shows 1xx lower error rate so far.

sasha: observed 503 -> 200 transition for canary after 3 minutes. pushing 30% slowly. monitoring.

support-ops: still seeing some customers with degraded throughput for embeddings and long-form generation; we've applied rate-limited retries for clients on the edge.

lee: long-term: we should pre-warm model caches on new nodes or use lazy loading with lower memory profile. Action item: add prefetch blocker + healthcheck that waits until KV cache warmed.

nora: sending external update: "Mitigation in progress. We've stabilized traffic to a subset of nodes and are rolling quantized model variants to reduce memory pressure. No data exposure. Next update in 15m."

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Incident acknowledged by sasha (on-call). Escalation status: active.

sasha: handing off to @lee for ongoing runtime tuning; I need to triage another page. Lee, context: autoscaler thrash -> daisy-chain node eviction -> container crashloops due to cold-model OOMs. Customer impact: elevated 5xx and lower throughput for some EU customers.

lee: got it. I'll coordinate with eng-runtime and eng-sre. tagging @devon for follow-up on model loading logic and @kyle for autoscaler policy review.

devon: opening follow-up ticket: ENG-RUNTIME-1243 "Model prewarm + low-mem bootstrap to prevent cold-start OOMs" and assigning to eng-runtime.

kyle: opening infra ticket: ENG-SRE-546 "Autoscaler damping and scale policy hardening" and assigning to eng-sre.

nora: internal postmortem note: potential root cause = aggressive autoscaler thresholds + heavy model cold-start memory usage causing crashloop cascade -> capacity thrash. Recommend: 1) scale damping defaults 2) model prewarm + KV warm healthchecks 3) make quantized fallback route configurable by region 4) set autorecovery window vs removal window.

support-ops: customer comms posted. no high-severity SLA breaches yet, but we have at-risk accounts. creating follow-ups for any customers with extended impact.

lee: monitoring 5xx trend: dropping from +300% to +45% over 18 minutes. continuing to observe. will update when stable.

infra-bot: resolution-check scheduled in 30m.

sasha: thanks team. leaving note here for next handoff: if oscillation recurs, immediately pin autoscaler to conservative mode and shift traffic to dedicated stable-pool; avoid full drain of evicted nodes until model caches released.

lee: agreed. closing active paging loop for now, moving to incident tracking workspace and postmortem.

devon: assigning ENG-RUNTIME-1243 -> priority P1 for sprint next week.

nora: saving logs/commands here for postmortem. will compile a timeline for RCA.

support-ops: updating ticket refs in customer threads.

pagerduty: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring.

lee: last check: latency and errors trending down. I will run a TTL-72h watch to ensure no recurrence.

sasha: thanks all, handing back to oncall rotation. :thumbsup:
